title: Lichfield Health weekly pilot performance gate sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review latency/throughput benchmarks vs incumbent baseline. Redwood shows lower median and p95 latencies in light-to-moderate load, higher throughput in continuous-batch tests; tail latency under sustained bursts needs tuning. Security and VPC requirements noted. Next steps: share raw bench logs, run stress test with prefix cache enabled, customer to share traffic profile and test corpus.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samira, Diego, Marta / Rajiv, Aisha, Tom

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — go over the sprint bench, call out where we beat the baseline and where we saw gaps, brainstorm quick tunings, and align on next steps.
00:12 Rajiv: Thanks Samira. We'll be brief, we've got an engineering all hands after.
00:18 Diego: Awesome. I'll start with the numbers — note these are from the 4/30 lab run against model v2.1, which is the same model the incumbent used but with our dynamic batch and continuous-kv settings.
00:34 Diego: Median latency across our synthetic traces is 78 ms, p95 is 140 ms under their mid-tier load (60 rps). Baseline provider numbers from their last report were median 125 ms, p95 230 ms, so pretty substantial delta.
00:50 Aisha: Wait, those are median numbers — what's the long tail when you spike to 200 rps?
00:57 Diego: Good call — under sustained 200 rps burst the p99 drifted to ~1.2s on our setup, the baseline hit ~1.8s. So we keep a lead but tail latency grows.
01:13 Tom: What about throughput — raw RPS before we see degrade?
01:18 Diego: In our throughput soak, with batching tuned we sustained ~460 rps at 40 tokens average before token queueing started to add latency. Baseline plateaued near 330 rps on the same vCPU/GPU mix they reported.
01:33 Rajiv: Are these numbers from Hosted or Dedicated? We need to map to our production plan — we're leaning VPC private infra.
01:41 Samira: These were on Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) in us-west. Diego can speak to how the Private deployment performed in the lab when we ran it inside a VPC.
01:49 Diego: Right — on Redwood Privatee (note: audio transcription error) inside a VPC with network egress policies, median/p95 were roughly +10% over Dedicated; so median ~86 ms p95 ~155 ms, mainly networking and encryption overhead.
02:08 Aisha: That's acceptable if it's predictable. Our security folks will want KMS integration and audit logs.
02:13 Marta: We'll send the SOC2 + ISO artifacts and the KMS HSM integration doc after this call — noted in next steps.
02:20 Tom: Back to performance — you mentioned KV/prefix caching. How much did that help?
02:27 Diego: The prefix KV cache cut p95 by about 27% on conversational traces that have repeated context. For spawning inference (stateless single-turn) it didn't move the needle much. Also continuous batching — we saw a 15% unit-cost reduction vs naive per-request processing.
02:45 Rajiv: When you say unit-cost reduction, is that tokens or dollars? Give me dollars.
02:50 Diego: With our current config, unit token cost was about 18% lower than baseline when both used FP16. With q4 quant, cost delta widened to 32% but note quality tradeoffs — we ran evaluation on the customer prompt set and saw a small ROUGE drop for certain prompt families.
03:12 Aisha: That quality drop is a red flag for the clinical-extraction flows. We cannot lose precision.
03:18 Diego: Understood — this is why we recommended mixed strategy: quantize for non-critical routes (embeddings, general summarization) and keep FP16 for named-entity extraction flows. Also we can pin model variants per route in the rollout.
03:33 Tom: Any stability anomalies during the run? Crashes, OOMs?
03:38 Diego: No crashes. We saw occasional KV cache misses after long idle periods that caused a ~200 ms spike — likely TTL warms. We have a warm-up policy that can be enabled to preload keys for hot routes.
03:52 Rajiv: Can you replay the logs for us? We want to map that to our traffic shape.
03:57 Samira: Yes we'll share the raw bench logs and the trace visualizations — Diego will annotate hotspots.
04:03 Diego: Quick note — the comparative tests used the same tokenization and sequence length distributions, but the baseline's reported numbers exclude certain pre/post-processing steps; when we add those the gap narrows about 5-7%. So be careful with apples-to-apples.
04:22 Rajiv: Good to know. What about routing and fallback — you have policies we can lean on?
04:28 Marta: Yes, we have smart routing where you can set latency and cost thresholds and fallback to a cheaper model variant or a different region. That was how we kept overall error budget low in the 200 rps spike tests.
04:40 Aisha: Does fallback keep user-visible latency SLOs? It won't silently change the output format?
04:46 Diego: We support function-calling and structured output; fallback respects the schema. If you fallback to a smaller model we recommend a quick post-processing validation step in the service layer — we provide hooks for that.
04:59 Tom: Any security tradeoffs with fallback (e.g., sending data to another region)?
05:04 Samira: Fallback can be constrained by policy — you can disable cross-region fallback, or allow only models hosted in private deployments with KMS.
05:13 Rajiv: Okay. About the tail latency under burst — is there a tuning we can try quickly?
05:18 Diego: Two immediate knobs: increase background warm-up (keeps KV cache hot) and tune continuous batching window to bias for latency at the cost of some throughput. We can also enable prefix caching for sessionized flows which cuts tail.
05:32 Rajiv: Let's try warm-up and prefix cache first.
05:36 Diego: We'll also run a 1-hour stress with an 80% sustained load and 30s spikes to replicate your real traffic. That will give us p99 and p999 visibility.
05:45 Aisha: When can you run that? We can give you a replay corpus.
05:48 Diego: We can start on 2027-05-07 morning PDT if you deliver the corpus by 5/6.
05:55 Rajiv: We'll aim to deliver the corpus and traffic profile by 5/6.
06:00 Samira: Great. Switching to cost: based on the sample traffic you shared, projected monthly inference cost on Dedicated is ~$21k vs baseline ~$28.5k, assuming the same traffic and 30% caching effectiveness. This is a back-of-envelope to get you started.
06:20 Tom: That cost delta matters. How much of that is quantization assumptions?
06:24 Diego: Quantization accounts for a chunk — moving from FP16 to q4 reduced token compute by ~25% in our numbers, but again the quality constraints will determine where you can apply it.
06:36 Rajiv: Any production incidents with other customers after similar tuning?
06:40 Marta: We've had a handful where caching policies were too aggressive and caused stale contexts; fixed via TTL and pre-warm rules. Also we had one case of misrouted fallback when region constraints were not set — all ops-level configs now have safety overrides.
06:56 Tom: Let's talk about audit/security docs. We'll need: SOC2 Type II, network architecture diagram for VPC Private, KMS integration spec, and an SLA digest.
07:07 Marta: We'll bundle those. Expect a secure share link by EOD 5/04.
07:14 Aisha: Also need packet timing for the lab runs — latency breakdown by hop if possible.
07:19 Diego: We'll include per-stage timing: ingress, tokenize, model, kv/cache, egress. I have a visual that shows the breakdown.
07:27 Rajiv: Competitors in our RFP were ModelHub and Infralytix — ModelHub had better batch throughput but worse p95 in small-context chats, Infralytix had lower unit cost but poor caching features.
07:44 Samira: Noted. We'll include a short competitive note in the handoff.
07:49 Tom: Alright, let's capture explicit next steps and owners.
07:53 Samira: I'll read them out. First — Samira: share benchmark spreadsheet, raw logs, and the annotated trace visuals.
07:59 Diego: Diego: run 1-hr 80% load stress test with prefix cache and warm-ups enabled, capture p99/p999, and log per-stage timings.
08:09 Rajiv: Rajiv: deliver replay corpus and traffic profile by 2027-05-06.
08:15 Aisha: Aisha: security team to review the SOC2 + network doc; we'll schedule a security call if anything flags.
08:22 Marta: Marta: provide SOC2/ISO docs, KMS integration spec, SLA digest by EOD 2027-05-04.
08:29 Tom: Tom: internal decision meeting on 2027-05-10 to finalize pilot gating — we'll invite you.
08:36 Samira: Great. Anything else?
08:39 Rajiv: One micro item — can you include cost projections for a 3-region deployment if we enable disaster fallback?
08:44 Diego: Yes, we'll add a 3-region cost column with delta per-region and estimate incremental latency per region hop.
08:51 Samira: OK I'll recap and we'll follow up in email. Thanks all.
08:56 End of call.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "Privatee"), filler words and overlaps present, speaker labels sometimes generic.
